published_rung_replicate.why_here: W3_MESH_NOISE_FLOOR_RESULTS.md measured the mesh-generation scatter falling as N^-2 on the NACA 0012, so the replicate worth running first is at the COARSEST rung -- and the coarsest rung that matters is the one a credential is printed from. published_rung_replicate.method: Two cases from this body's own production case: A at the stored background divisions (the control, which must reproduce the stored cell count) and B perturbed. Every other file byte-identical. Both solved at 4 MPI ranks, scotch, so the pair shares one decomposition.
published_rung_replicate.finding: The scatter is 138.8x this body's own iterative 2-sigma, so it is cleanly separable and real, and it is 7.4 percent of the envelope this row publishes. Whatever else is wrong with publishing an envelope off a declined ladder -- that is the open ruling w3-a-declined-ladder-still-publishes-an-envelope -- this envelope is NOT too small for the mesh scatter underneath it. That is a check the wall passed, and it is the first time it has been made. Read with this record's own band_rel of 0.70962 in view: the envelope is 71 percent of the value it decorates, and an envelope that large will contain almost anything.

recipe_audit.basis: audited 2026-08-14, tree at b14356b0, at NO COMPUTE: nothing was meshed, solved or refitted; every reading below comes off an archived log or dictionary. Basis: PRIMARY -- each rung's own archived log.snappyHexMesh, plus the coarse rung's own scaled background dictionary.
recipe_audit.cause: sdk/workflows/geometry_study.py, refinement_rungs(), introduced at fb0bf4a7 on 2026-07-24 and unmodified since, which is before this study was written. The generated path runs refinement=3, so base=3, medium_level=max(2,2)=2 and coarse_level=max(2,1)=2: the floor collapses the coarse level onto the medium level, which is the condition that gives the coarse rung, and only the coarse rung, block_scale 0.7. The production mesh is the case's own, at surface (3 4) / region 2. So a generated three-rung ladder is TWO recipes: coarse->medium moves the background blockMesh and holds the near-body levels fixed, medium->production moves the near-body levels and holds the background blockMesh identical. The runtime guard checks that the cell budgets are DISTINCT. Distinctness is not comparability, and nothing downstream was ever asked whether the rungs were comparable. Identical in kind to the finding already recorded on naca0012_wing.json, naca4412_wing.json, ahmed_25.json and ahmed_35.json.
recipe_audit.knob_moved: two knobs across three rungs, one per step
recipe_audit.finding: The three stored rungs are TWO mesh recipes. The near-body refinement level is 1 for coarse and 1 for medium and 2 for production, read from each rung's own log.snappyHexMesh line 'Refinement level N for all cells inside nearBody' (mission-output/geometry-study/study-naca0015_sail-coarse, -medium, and study-naca0015_sail). The background blockMesh differs between coarse and medium and is IDENTICAL between medium and production: the level-0 entry of each log's 'Cells per refinement level' histogram reads 39900, 116640 and 116640. The coarse rung's own blockMeshDict.scaled is archived beside its log and reads hex (42 25 38) = 39900, against the production system/blockMeshDict's (60 36 54) = 116640 -- ratios 0.700, 0.694, 0.704, which is refinement_rungs()'s block_scale 0.7 on the coarse rung and nothing else. So coarse and medium share one refinement recipe and differ only in background density, which IS a uniform refinement; production changes the near-body level and is not extrapolation-comparable to either.
